guidance: Planning estimate—verify assumptions and important results before committing time or money.
method: A speed conform keeps every frame and plays the clip at the target rate, so the playback factor is target fps divided by source fps: 24 to 25 fps runs at 1.0417x, 4.17% faster. The frame count is duration x source fps rounded to the nearest whole frame, the conformed duration is that frame count divided by the target rate, and the same-length alternative reports how many frames a frame-for-frame conform would duplicate (target rate higher) or drop (target rate lower). Audio that is not retimed shifts by 12 x log2(target / source) semitones, with no pitch correction applied. Inputs are limited to 1-240 fps and 0.1-86,400 s; frame rates within 0.002 fps of 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97 and 30 are treated as the named rate for the PAL and 0.1% pull-up notes. Drop-frame timecode, interlaced field order, 3:2 pulldown, motion blur and any pitch-correcting retime are not modelled, whole-frame rounding matters for very short clips, and a clip that rounds to zero frames at the source rate is rejected. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
